newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas crashes on low offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas crashes on low offers.

text.p: Gasoline prices crashed by more than $1.00 per barrel as the market returned from its holiday full of aggressive sellers, traders said.

Offers for unleaded 95-octane cargoes lifting in April started at $27.90 per barrel but a Swiss trader offered it down to as low as $27.00, where a European major bought the 50,000 barrels lifting April 15-19. On Thursday, the grade was talked more than a $1.00 higher at $28.00/$28.10.
"Maybe they are trying to sell before the crash," one trader tried to explain. " There are a lot of barrels coming in...two cargoes from Yanbu in first and second half April."
"It (market) is slightly longer," agreed another trader. "Besides Taiwan, there is more surplus than demand."
Taiwan's tender to buy 500,000 barrels of leaded and unleaded 95-octane for delivery in May 1-15, closes Tuesday and is valid for two days.
But in the mid-term, traders expect May to be better supported with the start of the US driving season and Asian refinery turnarounds.
Naphtha April swaps were talked about 20 cents firmer at $23.10/$23.30.

But discussion on Singapore barrels was thin with only India emerging with two tenders to sell 30,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha (LAN) from Bombay and 25,000 tonnes from Vizag, both lifting mid-April, industry sources said.
Both tenders close April 3 and are valid until April 4.

IOC's last LAN cargo from Bombay lifting February 20-22 was awarded at $23.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob, while its last Vizag LAN cargo, lifting March 30-April 1 was awarded to European major Shell at $17.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob.
